cells.tense: The practice is lit right now and the person is at the desk with it.
cells.ask: Before the next session, write down one feeling that keeps arriving and one you keep setting aside, then treat both the same for a week.
cells.core:
The practice is burning steady and you are at the desk with it. Most days it is one person, one feeling at a time, and you keep it honest. You feel the whole of a thing and then set it down level, and that is rare. What you have built holds up under weight, and the proof is that it doesn't need an audience.

What is free to grow from here is the part that lets go. You know how to keep a practice. You are less practiced at letting a season of it end and starting the next one without ceremony. Feed the endings. Let one old routine go by choice, out loud to yourself, and let the next thing be small. Fairness inside you stays clear when you let it turn over. The next step is a release, not another thing to hold.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the practice fair and steady. Now let one part of it end.

cells.tense: The mind is already at the next session before this one has finished.
cells.ask: Pick the one practice that matters most this week and do it exactly as written, same length, same steps, no additions.
cells.core:
You are already inside the next session while this one is still going. Somewhere ahead there is a version where it is finally fair, finally right, and you are rehearsing for it. The practice becomes a courthouse. Every feeling gets weighed, compared, sentenced. You feel the case building before the feeling has even landed.

What that costs is the plain thing the practice was for. Fairness turns into arithmetic. You check the ledger so often the exchange stops flowing. The way back is not more precision. It is holding what you have without squeezing it. Let one rule stand for a week and do not revise it. The strength here is what contains rather than what presses. You are closer than the rehearsal makes you feel.

cells.tense: The practice has gone quiet and the person is still standing behind it.
cells.ask: Set a timer for ten minutes and do the smallest version of the practice, then write one honest sentence about what you noticed.
cells.core:
The desk is there and the practice has gone quiet. Not abandoned, just not entered. The room got heavy and you stopped coming in, and at the time that made sense. Now the practice waits, and you circle it, and the circling is the habit. The feeling you used to weigh is still arriving. You are just not at the desk when it does.

What is missing is not fairness. It is the small repeated act that used to make fairness possible. Ten minutes, one honest sentence, that is enough to start. Inquiry does not demand feeling first. It just asks you to look, and looking is its own warmth. Start smaller than feels worth it. The point is not the practice. The point is that you show up where it happens.

cells.tense: The judgment is already running and it is being described as just being sensible.
cells.ask: Next time you call a feeling unreasonable, say out loud that you are the one making that call.
cells.core:
You are already weighing what is fair. It runs through your days. You can tell when something is disproportionate before you name it, and you can tell what is owed and what is not. Yet the call gets described as if the situation itself made it. The judgment is running. Nobody has signed it.

Under it is a simpler thing, one you already have: the ability to notice without deciding. That is the younger version of the same line, and it is the one to return to. Not a new skill, not more practice. Just watching a feeling arrive before you rule on it. Building the ability is not the work. The work is to stop handing it to the room.
cells.sheetLine: You are already judging what is fair. You keep calling it the situation.
